g.text: MEAT
THE BIBLE’S
SYMBOLIC
LANGUAGE
DANIEL LARIMER
Over 140 symbols revealed
DANIEL
LARIMER
“I fed you with milk and not with meat;
for until now you were not able to receive it,
and even now you are still not able.”
1 Corinthians 3:2
By this time you ought to be eating meat.
The wise and faithful servant gives the household
“meat in due season,” becomes a “steward of the
mysteries of God,” and has his senses “exercised
to discern” all parables. Would Jesus rebuke you
as he did his disciples: “Know ye not this parable?

text.tspan: and how then will ye know all parables?”

g.text: This book feeds meat — not a closed set of mysteries
explained, but lessons in how to seek and discover
fresh meat on your own. With more than 140 symbols
proved from Scripture’s own cross-references, it
brings the Bible to life.
Come — meet the Bible’s symbolic language.
“For everyone who partakes
only of milk is unskilled in the
word of righteousness,
for he is a babe.”
Hebrews 5:13
“And there are also many other
things that Jesus did, which if
they were written one by one,
I suppose that even the world
itself could not contain the books
that would be written.”
John 21:25
TIMETESTED.BIBLE
The book ends; the study doesn’t.
An interactive edition of this book
lives at TimeTested.Bible — every
quote and citation linked straight to
the Scriptures, with complete
interlinear tools to help you move
from milk to meat.
Pull every reference by key word, by the
Hebrew or Greek beneath the English,
and by concept — what once took a
lifetime of concordance work now takes
minutes.
Download the ebook free, and have
your friends and family meet the
Bible’s symbolic language.
Take no man’s word — verify.
ALSO BY DANIEL LARIMER
TIME TESTED TRADITION
The Renewed Biblical Calendar
When is the Sabbath? The calendar
the Scriptures keep, recovered from
the text itself — the renewed moon,
the appointed feasts, and the count
that convicts every alternative.
Read it free at TimeTested.Bible.
